audit.method: source dependency/allocation audit plus cProfile and pre-edit wall samples

methodology.machine: local Linux x86_64; same checkout and Python environment

dependency_map.traversal: all functions/blocks/instructions and operand ownership occurrences
dependency_map.allocations: fresh normalized IR when expansion is needed
dependency_map.complexity: linear in IR plus lifecycle bookkeeping

dependency_map.recomputed: once for lowering; verifier builds an SSA CFG independently

dependency_map.recomputed: lowering and independent verifier each compute their own

dependency_map.representation: before: dict[str,set[str]] full sets; after: source-indexed Python integer bit masks
dependency_map.allocations: before copied full sets and intersections; after C-level integer AND results
dependency_map.recomputed: once in lowering and once in verifier
dependency_map.complexity: same dataflow convergence; representation drops Python-object relation materialization

dependency_map.representation: before enumerated every strict dominator; after bit-count depth buckets
dependency_map.traversal: before O(materialized dominance relation); after one depth-mask intersection per block
dependency_map.allocations: before strict set per block; after depth mask per tree depth
dependency_map.complexity: before quadratic on linear CFG; after O(blocks) big-int operations

dependency_map.traversal: one idom edge per reachable non-entry block
dependency_map.allocations: one child set per block frozen once

dependency_map.recomputed: pre-change reachability was redundantly recomputed; after it reuses the independent Python dominator result

dependency_map.allocations: new in/out sets per changed transfer

dependency_map.recomputed: definitions are scanned separately from liveness and placement

dependency_map.representation: slot to block-name sets and deque worklists
dependency_map.traversal: iterated dominance frontier per defined slot
dependency_map.allocations: placed/seen sets and worklist per slot
dependency_map.recomputed: frontier immutable views are now reused without a copy

dependency_map.representation: name dictionaries, per-slot stacks, iterative ENTER/EXIT frames
dependency_map.allocations: mutation logs per entered block; no recursive stack
dependency_map.recomputed: reachable set is validated again as a safety check
dependency_map.complexity: linear in visited IR plus phi incoming edges

dependency_map.representation: SSA object graph and independent verifier CFG/dominance
dependency_map.traversal: whole module; dominance is computed again for verification
dependency_map.recomputed: not duplicate verification: this is the builder's required single verification

dependency_map.allocations: final SSA containers and phi tuples

phase_profiles.dominant_before_deep: builder verification (including its independent full-set dominance), then builder idom derivation/dominance
phase_profiles.dominant_after_deep: lifecycle normalization, builder verification, then renaming
phase_profiles.dominant_before_ordinary: lifecycle normalization and builder verification; dominance was not an ordinary-workload hotspot
phase_profiles.dominant_after_ordinary: lifecycle normalization and builder verification; definite initialization and renaming follow

deep_cfg.before_reason: 5000 blocks required 6.58 s Python-only and 1.31 GiB peak RSS; the required nine 10000-block passes were not safe/practical

memory.method: fresh process resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss after one 5000-block build
memory.note: old relation count alone is a 100,020,000-byte pointer lower bound before Python set table overhead

independence.python_algorithm: iterative full-dominator-set dataflow represented by Python integer masks
independence.shared_bug_class: representation/index mapping bugs remain possible, but the fixed-point equations and idom derivation differ from Rust CHK
independence.guard: tests reject Rust process/FFI imports and chk_idom coupling in the production Python implementation

answers.deep_dominant_before: Python full-set dominance/idom in lowering and verifier
answers.deep_dominant_after: lifecycle normalization and verification; renaming is next in lowering
answers.dominance_full_set_iteration: semantic full-set fixed point retained, Python set objects removed from the hot path
answers.dominance_materialization: 5000-block linear relation has 12,502,500 memberships; measured process peak fell from 1,375,420 to 93,604 KiB
answers.definite_initialization_expensive: material on realistic ordinary code, not dominant on the one-slot deep linear fixture
answers.renaming_expensive: third largest deep lowering component after lifecycle/verification
answers.liveness_frontier_repeated: frontier reachability was redundant and removed; liveness runs once
answers.copies: frontier/tree child copies removed for internal consumers
answers.integer_indexes: used only compilation-locally; names remain external
answers.verification_vs_lowering: before deep CFG verification exceeded lowering's individual dominance phases; after it remains one of the two largest end-to-end phases

qualification.production_stabilization_detail: 3 repeated corpus rounds, 5000-request persistent session, 256 concurrent requests
